mainEntity.name: When should a family consider building multigenerational living quarters?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many households build additional living quarters to accommodate aging parents, adult children moving home, or frequent out-of-town visitors. If you are experiencing daily friction over shared bathrooms, lack of quiet workspace, or caregiving challenges, an independent suite provides privacy while keeping loved ones close. It is also a practical consideration when family members require accessible living features, such as zero-threshold walk-in showers and step-free entries, which can be difficult to retrofit into an existing second-story bedroom. An addition offers customized space tailored to long-term family stability.
acceptedAnswer.description: Consider an addition when caring for aging parents, housing adult children, or needing ground-floor accessible living with dedicated private bath and kitchen amenities.
